title: Batching Pays for the Flush Once
subtitle: kvdb with F_FULLFSYNC on every commit, N random puts per WriteBatch, one run per row

rows.label: 1 put per batch
rows.detail: 2,000 puts. Median commit 4.01 ms, p99 6.10 ms. Load average 5.1

rows.label: 4 puts per batch
rows.detail: 2,000 puts. Median commit 4.00 ms, p99 6.06 ms. Load average 5.1

rows.label: 16 puts per batch
rows.detail: 2,000 puts. Median commit 4.01 ms, p99 4.98 ms. Load average 5.1

rows.label: 64 puts per batch
rows.detail: 1,984 puts (31 batches). Median commit 4.00 ms, max 7.02 ms. Load average 5.1

rows.label: 256 puts per batch
rows.detail: 1,792 puts (7 batches). Median commit 4.05 ms, max 6.03 ms. Load average 5.1

caption: The median commit stays at about 4 ms whatever the batch size, so throughput grows almost exactly with the number of puts that share one flush. The 64 and 256 rows rest on 31 and 7 commits, so their tails are thin. Shared Apple M4 Pro at a 1 minute load average of 5.1, indicative only.
